text:
Alex: Heads-up — since the kernel-affinity + adaptive-queue rollout last night I'm seeing p95 spike for small requests on cont-batching. p95 up ~220ms, overall throughput down ~7%. Anyone else seeing this?

Maria: saw the alert this morning. Quick glance at the dashboard shows a KV cache hit-rate drop in the same window (was ~91% -> ~78%). Suspect interaction between affinity and cache eviction.

Jia: digging into profiler now. Early hypothesis: affinity is pushing tiny requests to a narrow kernel optimized for long sequences; batching then waits for token budget targets and misses small-KV-hot paths.

Simone: hmm that would explain the tail behaviour. The new queue-adaptivity also increases target wait time for groups <8 tokens which could be compounding latency.

PerfBot: alert: cont-batcher.p95 increased 220ms (obs window 02:00-04:00), throughput -7.6%. kv_cache.hit_rate dropped 13.2% during same interval.

Alex: Jia, can you paste the top of the CPU profile? Even a quick `pprof` dump will help.

Jia: paste from staging profile run (representative):

```
# pprof top
Total samples: 10000
  kernel_selector           430  43.0%  # affinity selection cost
  batching_queue           210  21.0%  # queue wait & merge overhead
  kv_cache                 150  15.0%  # cache lookup + eviction churn
  dispatcher               120  12.0%  # dispatch to kernels
  gpu_executor              90   9.0%
```

Jia: interestingly `kernel_selector` went from ~18% before rollout to 43% now. That alone explains a lot of CPU time being spent deciding routes.

Maria: I ran flame graphs for a tail request that hit 1.2s p99: most time is in `kernel_selector::score_affinity` and then `kv_cache::evict_if_needed` due to eviction churn. Looks like affinity heuristics are increasing cache churn.

Simone: so two interacting effects: (1) affinity causes more packing into kernels that don't align with KV cache prefix locality -> lower hit rate; (2) queue-adaptivity increases waiting for tiny groups which lengthens latency.

Alex: Can we reproduce locally by toggling affinity off and toggling queue-adaptivity policy? If turning affinity off restores hit-rate and reduces kernel_selector time, we can rollback quickly.

Jia: repro steps I used:
```
# feature flags
PATCH /admin/flags {"kernel_affinity": false, "queue_adaptivity": "old"}
# run loadgen with tiny-req distribution
./loadgen --dist tiny --qps 300 --duration 10m
# capture perf
pprof -http=:6060 /tmp/profile.pb
```
I got p95 ~120ms and kv_cache hit ~90% when affinity is disabled. With affinity enabled p95 ~340ms and hit ~77%.

Maria: good repro. I'm +1 for rolling kernel_affinity to previous state in prod canary while we dig deeper. Queue-adaptivity change we can throttle in the next deploy window rather than immediate rollback.

Simone: agree. Also worth adding a small heuristic guard: if kv_cache.hit_rate drops >5% in a minute after affinity selection, fall back to old selector for that shard. Less risky than full rollback.

Alex: action plan:
- Maria will flip kernel_affinity -> old in canary (prod-canary-3) now.
- Jia will collect golden profiles (before/after) and annotate where eviction increases.
- Simone will prototype a short-circuit guard on selector if cache hit drops.
- I'll create a quick dashboard to track kernel_selector CPU, kv_cache.hit_rate, cont-batcher.p95 across shards.

Maria: flipping canary flag now. Will post confirmation.

PerfBot: Deploy flag change recorded: /admin/flags kernel_affinity=false @Maria 1864123502

Maria: canary metrics stabilizing — p95 back to ~130ms on canary, kv_cache hit restored to ~89%. Will monitor for 15m then we can decide to promote rollback to more shards.

Alex: great. Jia, please attach the two pprof captures to the ticket and label with `affinity-regression`. Simone, can you start a small PR for the short-circuit guard and link it here?

Jia: will attach profiles to ticket INF-1327. Quick note: we should also revisit the kernel scoring weights — currently favoring sequence-length can ignore cache locality score. I propose adding a small locality penalty term.

Simone: opening draft PR now: #4123 — adds cache-locality penalty and a runtime toggle. Tests included.

Alex: perfect. Let's keep cont-batching rollout paused until we have the locality term and the guard in canary. Thanks everyone.

Maria: noted. I'll keep monitoring and will update thread in 15m.
